paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. David's song starts with a steady heart and ends with a steady God. He says, "My heart is steadfast, O God," and then he sings about a love that "extends beyond the heavens" (Psalm 108:1, 4). Your heart can be steady because of who God is, and your mood has nothing to do with it.

Now look at the middle, because this is where it gets real. God says, "I will triumph!" and then David asks, "Have You not rejected us, O God?" (Psalm 108:7, 11). Friend, David held the promise and the hard question in the same song, and he kept right on praying. You can bring God your doubts too, because He can handle them, and a song that has questions in it is still a song.

So here's what I want you to take with you. David says, "the help of man is worthless," and then, "With God we will perform with valor" (Psalm 108:12, 13). When the road ahead feels like a fortified city, don't lean on yourself, because that's a shaky place to stand. Lean on God, sing to Him first thing in the morning, and let your steady heart come from Him.
